catalog_quote: Calon 1890: 501: "4°. De klemtoon valt altijd op de voorlaatste lettergreep; behalve als anders aangegeven wordt. 5°. Het teeken ´ boven eene lettergreep beteekent dat op die lettergreep den klemtoon valt." [Rules 1-3 and 6-7 on pp. 501-502 concern vowel length and vowel quality only.] Rosen 1986: 51: "STRESS. Word stress usually seems to fall on the first syllable and as far as I know is not phonemic." Rosen 1986: 49: "Although in the first minimal pair mo.á 'old man' : mó.a 'to yawn' above it appears that stress could be mutually exclusive with the murmuring of vowels, we can see from the pair áta 'to read' : áta 'person' that this is not the case. Although stress is usually on the first syllable in Maumere, it can apparently occasionally fall on other syllables." [In the pairs, the murmured vowels of mó.a, áta 'person' are printed underlined.]

new_statements.translation: 4. The stress always falls on the penultimate syllable, except where indicated otherwise. 5. The sign ´ above a syllable means that the stress falls on that syllable.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again. Opened (rendered from the archive.org volume PDF, leaf 524 of 626; the PDF has no text layer). The page is headed "WOORDENLIJSTJE van het DIALECT VAN SIKKA (MIDDEN-FLORES) verzameld door L. F. CALON" and carries numbered rules 1-6; rules 4 and 5 read exactly: "4°. De klemtoon valt altijd op de voorlaatste lettergreep; behalve als anders aangegeven wordt. 5°. Het teeken ´ boven eene lettergreep beteekent dat op die lettergreep den klemtoon valt." Verbatim as reported (the acute is printed as a small raised mark; the archive.org scanned at line 24398-24402 of the renders 4°/5° as "4^"/"5^" and drops the mark, which is why the page image is the authority). The…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is penultimate by default; the wordlist marks with an acute the (lexical) exceptions where stress falls elsewhere.
new_statements.exceptions: Exceptions exist and are marked individually in the wordlist with an acute over the stressed syllable; no rule for them is given. Calon 1893 (TBG 35, p. 128-129) adds that mountain dwellers say 'lahing' with penultimate stress where the coast has 'lahein'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms in a Dutch-Sikkanese wordlist compiled by the Maumere parish priest; the dialect is that of Sikka/Maumere on the south-central coast ('dialect van Sikka, Midden-Flores'). An 1890 missionary source, so orthography-driven and pre-phonemic; the modern descriptions (Rosen 1986, Lewis & Grimes 1995, Fricke 2014) could not be opened to confirm.
new_statements.identity_note: Calon's 1890 wordlist describes the coastal Sikka/Maumere dialect ('dialect van Sikka, Midden-Flores'; Calon was parish priest at Maumere), i.e. sika1262 proper; Lewis 1982 (opened, no stress statement) treats the Tana Ai dialect (Sara Tana Ai) and Fricke 2014 (not opened) the Hewa variety, both sub-dialects of the same glottocode with no separate Glottolog languoid.
